benchmark_note: External consensus is not unique: a current economic calendar shows 55.2 while Morningstar reported a 55.8 FactSet consensus on Aug. 28. Both are frozen rather than selecting one after the outcome. No later consensus will be retrofitted.
resolution_rule: Use the first Institute for Supply Management Manufacturing PMI report released 2026-09-01 at 10:00 ET. Resolve TRUE if the August 2026 headline Manufacturing PMI is 55.0 or higher at ISM's published one-decimal precision; otherwise FALSE. Score the 0.42 probability with Brier and log loss. Score the 54.4 point estimate by absolute error against the frozen 55.6 no-change, 55.2 current-calendar, and 55.8 FactSet point benchmarks. Record whether the realized value lies inside the 51.0-57.5 80% interval. Do not substitute later revisions or a consensus captured after the evidence cutoff.
rationale: July ISM Manufacturing PMI was 55.6, providing a strong same-series anchor, but the Aug. 21 national flash manufacturing PMI was softer at 53.2.

Aug. 31 regional evidence is sharply conflicting: Dallas Fed production/new orders accelerated while Chicago PMI fell to 47.1. The v0.2.8 error-linked safeguard says regional headlines should not be linearly extrapolated into a national manufacturing index.

The forecast therefore places the >=55 event below even odds and below external point consensuses without making a high-confidence contraction call. It deliberately preserves a wide enough interval for survey-method and regional-composition differences while remaining sharper than the system's very broad legacy macro intervals.

This forecast is designed to test whether the regional-to-national bridge correction improves subsequent national-manufacturing forecasting; it receives no learning credit until resolved and compared with frozen benchmarks.
surprising_if: The first-release ISM Manufacturing PMI is >=58.0, implying much stronger national carry-through from July/regional strength than the forecast distribution allows.
The first-release ISM Manufacturing PMI is <=50.0, implying a much sharper national manufacturing deterioration than current national and regional evidence suggests.
source_notes: ISM's release calendar states Manufacturing PMI is released on the first business day of the month at 10:00 a.m. ET and lists September 1 for the September 2026 release cycle.
ISM's July 2026 report recorded Manufacturing PMI at 55.6.
Dallas Fed's Aug. 31 Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey recorded production 16.1 and new orders 22.0.
Current Chicago PMI calendar reporting recorded August at 47.1 versus 57.6 prior; its duplicate date labeling is a data-quality caution, not a basis for changing the value.
External point consensus snapshots disagree (55.2 current calendar; 55.8 FactSet via Morningstar), so both are frozen prospectively.
